plainTranslation:
This can feel like finding someone whose mind moves at your speed.

The attraction is often mental first. Conversation starts quickly and may become exciting almost immediately. One person makes a leap, the other catches it. One says something strange or unexpected, and instead of being confused, the other adds to it. That can feel rare.

There is a kind of intimacy in being understood this quickly. You do not have to slow yourself down as much. You do not have to make every idea acceptable before saying it. With this person, your mind may feel freer, sharper, and more willing to say what it usually edits.

At its best, this connection can produce real breakthroughs. You may think better together than apart. One of you brings the sudden insight. The other helps give it language. Together, you can turn a strange idea into something other people can actually understand.

The challenge is staying with one thing long enough to finish it.

The conversation can be so stimulating that commitment to one idea starts to feel boring. You may keep chasing the next flash instead of building anything with the one you already had. A hundred ideas can pass between you and still leave nothing real behind.

There can also be nervous tension here. Too much talking, too much stimulation, too many new angles at once can make both people feel wired. Emotional conversations can suffer too. When a feeling comes up, it may be easier to turn it into a theory than to actually sit with it.

What helps is giving the energy a body. Talk while you walk. Cook while you brainstorm. Write things down. Pick one idea and see it through.

The brilliance is already there. The work is finishing.
